user.title: VTherm Smart Boiler
user.description: Monitors your boiler; it writes nothing to the boiler until you enable control in the options. Pick a name and the level of detail.

data_description.name: Shown as the device name.
data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials with cautious defaults; advanced shows every parameter. The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves.

signals.title: Boiler signals
signals.description: Pick the entity that provides each signal. Flame and flow temperature are required; every other signal enables more of the monitor. The plugin only reads these entities.

data_description.flame: On while the burner burns. Every burner-cycle metric comes from it: the wrong entity gives wrong starts and burn times.
data_description.flow: Water leaving the boiler. Used for hot water availability, emitter power and telling DHW runs from heating; with control, it is part of the boiler link. The wrong entity misleads all of them.
data_description.return: Water coming back to the boiler. Enables the condensing share; without it condensing cannot be judged. The wrong entity gives a wrong condensing share.
data_description.modulation: Burner modulation in percent. With the boiler's power range it estimates heat output and gas use. A sensor in another unit is refused.
data_description.dhw_active: On while the boiler heats domestic hot water. Without it DHW runs are inferred with less certainty and some may count as heating; with control, hot-water charging is then less sure to pause learning.
data_description.pressure: Enables the pressure alarms and the falling-pressure warning. The wrong entity gives false alarms or none.
data_description.outdoor: The boiler's own outdoor sensor. Used for degree-days, for control's curve, and checked against the weather entity: one found stuck or far off is left out of the curve. A wrong sensor bends the curve until the check catches it.
data_description.ch_setpoint: The flow setpoint the boiler works to, a temperature. Helps tell DHW runs from heating.
data_description.ch_active: On while the boiler heats the rooms. Helps tell DHW from heating when there is no DHW signal.
data_description.pump_running: On while the heating pump runs. Enables the low-flow warning: every valve closed while the pump runs.
data_description.flue_gas: Enables the flue gas alarm and the early warning of a fouling heat exchanger.
data_description.gas_meter: A cumulative gas or energy meter. Gives measured gas per degree-day instead of an estimate.
data_description.room_setpoint: The room setpoint a wired thermostat sends to the boiler, if there is one. Recorded for the assessment.
data_description.room_temperature: The room temperature a wired thermostat sends to the boiler, if there is one. Recorded for the assessment.
data_description.weather: Its forecasts are recorded for later forecast features, and its temperature stands in for a missing or suspect outdoor sensor — for degree-days and control's curve. No data leaves your Home Assistant.

boiler.title: Boiler
boiler.description: What you know about your boiler. Leave unknown values empty: the plugin then says what it cannot judge.

data.class: What the boiler's integration can do

data_description.class: Flow setpoint, curve parameters only, on/off or read-only. Control (experimental) needs "Flow setpoint"; with the other classes the plugin only monitors.
data_description.dhw: None, a storage tank or a combi boiler; required. Used to interpret burns: with "none" every burn counts as heating — declared on a boiler that heats hot water, its draws would count as heating starts; the wrong type counts hot water as heating or the reverse.
data_description.condensing: Condensing boilers get flue gas limits for condensing appliances and are judged on how often they condense; for other boilers the absolute flue gas alarm is off and condensing plays no part in the verdict. The wrong choice warns too late or for nothing, and misjudges the verdict.
data_description.boiler_min_power: Lowest heating power from the manual, in kW. Compared with the building load: a load often below it means the boiler must cycle. A wrong value skews that judgement in the verdict.
data_description.boiler_max_power: Highest heating power in kW. With the minimum and the modulation it estimates heat output; a wrong value skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.max_ch_setpoint: Highest flow temperature in heating, in °C. Flow above it points to a DHW run; set too low, heating counts as hot water. Control never writes a setpoint above it either: set too low, rooms stay cold in hard frost.
data_description.gas_at_min_power: Gas per hour at minimum power, in your gas meter's unit. With the modulation it estimates gas use when there is no meter; a wrong value skews gas per degree-day.
data_description.gas_at_max_power: Gas per hour at maximum power, in the same unit; a wrong value skews the gas estimates.
data_description.modulation_scale: Whether 0 % is the minimum power (the OpenTherm definition) or the value is a percentage of maximum power. The wrong choice skews heat and gas estimates.
data_description.bypass: Tick when the heating water always has a path — an automatic bypass valve or a low-loss header: the low-flow warning is then off, as closed valves cannot stop the flow. Left unticked on such a system, the warning is false; ticked without one, a real dead-end goes unwarned.

circuit.title: Heating circuit {number}
circuit.description: How this circuit's water temperature is set.

data_description.control: Unmixed, straight from the boiler; mixed through the boiler (a second circuit the boiler mixes); mixed by a separate controller; or a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed). Control runs only for one circuit fed straight from the boiler, or through a fixed valve. The wrong type makes control refuse, or misjudge what reaches the rooms.
data_description.max_flow: The most this circuit may receive, in °C, e.g. underfloor heating on an unmixed loop. Control treats it as a hard limit — the water never goes above it; underfloor heating on an unmixed loop needs it before control can run. Too high overheats the floor.
data_description.fixed_temperature: Needed for a thermostatic mixing valve (fixed): its setting in °C. Control keeps the boiler's flow at least this warm; set higher than the valve's setting, the water runs hotter than needed.
data_description.flow_entity: A mixed circuit's own flow temperature. Without it the heat reaching that circuit cannot be told.
data_description.add_another: Tick to describe one more circuit after this one.

zones.title: VT zones
zones.description: Pick the Versatile Thermostat zones heated by this boiler. Zones not picked are ignored.

data_description.zones: Only VT climate entities are offered. The plugin reads them; with control and learning pauses on, it also pauses and resumes their SmartPI learning. A zone left out neither calls for heat nor is watched for frost.

data_description.circuit: The heating circuit this zone is on. The wrong circuit attributes the zone's heat to the wrong water.
data_description.emitter: Radiators, underfloor or convectors. Sets the EN 442 exponent of the emitter power and the curve's default shape; the wrong type skews both.
data_description.foreign_heat: A fireplace, stove or electric heater in this room, not the sun: a switch or binary sensor that is on while it heats, or a power sensor (a temperature sensor at the advanced level, where its threshold is set). Shown as foreign heat for the zone; with control, its learning is paused meanwhile.
data_description.reference_output_w: The emitters' output at their reference condition, in W. Only for an absolute output estimate; a wrong value only skews that estimate.
data_description.exponent: Overrides the EN 442 exponent of the emitter type. A wrong exponent skews the emitter power factor.
data_description.power_threshold: A power source counts as heating above this, in W. Default 100 W. Too low counts standby as heating; too high misses a small heater.
data_description.temperature_threshold: Needed for a temperature source: it counts as heating above this, in °C. Too low counts a cold stove as heating; too high misses it.

building.title: Building
building.description: A first estimate of your house's heat loss; recorded heating days refine it. Leave empty what you do not know.

data_description.floor_area: In m². With the insulation class it gives a rough first estimate, replaced as data comes in; a wrong area skews the first days of the verdict.
data_description.insulation: Poor, average, good or very good. Part of the rough first estimate.
data_description.thermal_mass: How slowly the house cools. Recorded for later forecast features.
data_description.design_load_kw: Your own heat-loss calculation, in kW at the design outdoor temperature. Wins over the rough estimate; a value no house has is refused.
data_description.loss_coefficient: Heat loss per kelvin, in kW/K, if you know it. Wins over every estimate, measured ones included: a wrong value stays wrong.
data_description.heating_threshold: Outdoor temperature above which the house needs no heating, in °C; also the degree-day base. Default 15 °C. Wrong, degree-days and gas per degree-day are skewed.
data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature your design load refers to, in °C. Default −15 °C. Wrong, the estimate from your design load is skewed.

reference.title: Reference room
reference.description: One room temperature and setpoint for controllers that need a single room.

data_description.strategy: Largest deficit follows the room furthest below its setpoint; a chosen zone always uses one room; average uses every heating room. It is only published for external controllers; a chosen zone that is away leaves them without a reference.
data_description.zone: Used with the chosen-zone strategy. A room that is often off or away leaves the reference unknown.
data_description.switch_margin: Another room must be this much colder before the reference switches, in K. Smaller follows faster but switches more often, which can disturb an external controller.

data_description.condensing_return: A return below this counts as condensing, in °C. Default 55 °C. Too high overstates the condensing share.
data_description.short_burn_min: Burns shorter than this count as short, in minutes. Default 10. Longer makes more burns short, and the verdict harsher.
data_description.monitoring_days: Days of data before the verdict is given, and later before control can be enabled. Default 7; shorter is not allowed.
data_description.near_room_k: Water within this of the room counts as no hot water, in K. Default 3. Larger says 'no hot water' sooner.
data_description.foreign_heat_hold_min: How long a room still counts as warmed after its source stops, in minutes. Default 60. Longer keeps learning paused longer after a fire.
data_description.pressure_low_warning: Pressure below this raises a warning, in bar. Default 1.0. Take the value from your boiler's manual: too low warns too late.
data_description.pressure_low_alarm: Pressure below this raises an alarm, in bar. Default 0.7. Must be below the warning.
data_description.pressure_high_warning: Pressure above this raises a warning, in bar. Default 2.5. Too high warns too late.
data_description.pressure_high_alarm: Pressure above this raises an alarm, in bar. Default 2.8, below a typical 3 bar safety valve. Must be above the warning.
data_description.flue_gas_warning: Flue gas above this raises a warning on a condensing boiler, in °C. Default 85 °C. Too high warns too late.
data_description.flue_gas_alarm: Flue gas above this raises an alarm, in °C. Default 100 °C. A limit set too high warns too late for plastic flue pipes.
data_description.starts_per_hour_limit: More burner starts than this in an hour raise a warning. Default 12. Too high hides short-cycling.
data_description.unstable_burns_limit: More than this many burns under a minute in a day raise a warning. Default 10. Too high hides an ignition problem.
data_description.verdict_window_days: The verdict covers this many most recent days with data. Empty (default): every day kept, up to a year, filled at start from the recorder as far back as it reaches. Shorter follows a change in the house sooner; longer is steadier. It is never shorter than the monitoring period.

error.min_power_not_below_max: The minimum power must be below the maximum power.
error.fixed_temperature_missing: A thermostatic mixing valve (fixed) needs its temperature setting.
error.foreign_heat_unsupported: Only switches, binary sensors and power or temperature sensors can be heat sources.
error.temperature_threshold_missing: A temperature source needs a temperature threshold (advanced level).
error.reference_zone_unknown: Pick one of the configured zones.
error.implausible_parameter: A parameter is outside its plausible range.
error.unknown_circuit: A zone refers to a circuit that does not exist.
error.duplicate_circuit: Two circuits have the same name.
error.no_circuit: At least one circuit is needed.
error.invalid_control: The control settings cannot be used.
error.alarm_limits_out_of_order: An alarm limit must lie beyond its warning limit.
error.modulation_not_percent: Modulation is a percentage of the boiler's range: pick a sensor in %.

init.title: VTherm Smart Boiler options
init.description: Change one section; every other setting stays as it is.

menu_options.level_hidden: Level of detail (some hidden advanced settings are active)

level.title: Level of detail
level.description: The level changes only what you see, never how the plugin behaves.

data.restore_defaults: Restore advanced settings to their defaults

data_description.level: Simple shows the essentials; advanced shows every parameter.
data_description.restore_defaults: When switching to simple: tick to reset the advanced tuning — control's curve shape, limits and behaviour, the alarm reactions, the monitor's thresholds, the reference room's margin — to its defaults. Facts about your installation stay whatever you choose: mapped signals, the boiler, circuits, emitter sizes and values you entered. Left unticked, the tuning stays active but hidden, and the options show that some advanced settings are active.

freshness.title: Freshness limits
freshness.description: An age limit per signal, in minutes: a value not reported for longer counts as stale, for the monitor and for control alike — without a fresh flame and flow, control writes nothing and hands back after five minutes. Empty (default): only whether the entity is available counts, since many sources (MQTT among them) report only on change and a steady value is not a stale one. Risk: without a limit, a source that freezes without going unavailable is not caught; a limit shorter than a source's reporting interval stops control in steady weather.

control.title: Control (experimental)
control.description: How the plugin writes the flow setpoint to the boiler. Control stays off until you switch it on, and only after the monitoring period. Choose "No control" to keep monitoring only.

data_description.write_path: No control (default); a writable entity you pick, e.g. an EMS-ESP or ESPHome OpenTherm number; the OpenTherm Gateway through Home Assistant's OpenTherm Gateway integration; or the OTGW firmware's MQTT commands. Pick the path your boiler interface really offers: a wrong one means writes that fail or go nowhere.
data_description.topology: How the gateway sits between thermostat and boiler. With a thermostat: on hand-back the thermostat takes over. Stand-alone, without a thermostat: on hand-back, and whenever Home Assistant stops for more than about a minute, the boiler stops heating. Monitor mode: the gateway only listens and control is not possible. Virtual: a controller on the Home Assistant side, e.g. ESPHome, drives the boiler. Required; declare it as it is — the plugin never changes the gateway's mode. A lost link to the boiler's data raises an alarm and hands back in every topology — stand-alone, heating stops until the data returns.
data_description.confirmed_entity: The entity that reports the setpoint the boiler received, e.g. the gateway's "Control setpoint 1" on its boiler device — it shows what the gateway sends, so the setpoint is shown as confirmed by the gateway, not by the boiler. Required: every write is checked against it, and a write the boiler ignores or another controller overwrites is reported. The plugin's setpoint entity shows only a confirmed value, otherwise unknown. Picking the entity you write confirms nothing: the setpoint is then shown as unverified.
data_description.ch_confirmed_entity: Optional: an entity that reports whether the boiler receives heating enabled — e.g. the gateway's "Central heating 1" on its boiler device, which shows what the gateway sends to the boiler. With it, heating on/off is checked like the setpoint: a switch the boiler ignores is reported, and one another controller changes is written again once, then every write stops. Without it, heating on/off is shown as unverified and another controller switching it goes unnoticed. Picking the entity you write, or the thermostat's request instead of what the boiler receives, confirms nothing or stops control.
data_description.thermostat_setpoint_entity: Optional, for a gateway with an OpenTherm thermostat: the water temperature the thermostat itself asks for (with opentherm_gw, the thermostat device's "Control setpoint 1"), not the boiler's read-back. When the boiler falls back to it after an outage, the plugin sends its command again instead of taking it for another controller. Empty (default): only the value from before the plugin counts.
data_description.restart_entity: Optional: a sensor of the gateway or boiler interface that shows its restarts — an uptime that starts again from a low value, a restart counter that goes up, or a boot time (for example the OTGW firmware's reboot count, or an EMS-ESP or ESPHome uptime sensor). A restart it shows counts for 5 minutes as a trace of an outage: the boiler falling back to its own value then is taken as a lost command and simply sent again. Empty (default): a restart is seen only when the device's entities go unavailable, and a quick restart that shows nothing is judged as a fall-back without a trace — the first within an hour is still sent again, but a second may be taken for another controller, and the plugin steps aside.

control_entity.title: Writable entity
control_entity.description: The entity that takes the flow setpoint, and how control is handed back.

data_description.setpoint_entity: A number or input_number that sets the boiler's flow temperature.
data_description.write_type: Expiring: the device drops the value unless it is repeated; it is repeated every 30 s. Held: the device keeps the value and sends it on itself; written on change only. Persistent or unknown (default): stored in the boiler's memory, or it may be — the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory, so control is not available with such an entity. Risk: a stored parameter declared expiring would be written every 30 s, about 2,900 times a day, and wear the boiler's memory out.
data_description.ch_entity: Optional: a switch that turns heating on and off, turned back on at hand-back where the boiler returns to its own control or a thermostat, and left as it is where the hand-back stops heating; its write type is needed below. Without a switch, "off" is written as a low setpoint. Never pick a switch that is stored in the boiler's memory (e.g. a boiler's "heating activated" parameter): every switching would wear it. On must allow heating: a flag that stops heating while on (such as EMS-ESP's "heating off") turns every command round and must not be used here.
data_description.ch_write_type: Needed with a heating switch: what the device does with its state. Expiring: dropped unless repeated; repeated every 30 s. Held: the device keeps it. The plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory, so a switch declared persistent or unknown is refused.
data_description.hand_back: How control returns to the boiler on every exit. Every hand-back first writes the lowest water temperature, then turns the heating switch back on where the boiler returns to its own control or a thermostat, then follows the method chosen here: write a hand-back value; stop writing and let the device's own timeout take over, for expiring writes only; or turn off a switch that enables external control. Required; control cannot be switched on without it.
data_description.hand_back_value: The setpoint written on hand-back, in °C, for the value method: the value that returns the boiler to its own control, or the one it should keep. 0 means "own control" on some devices and "no heat" on others. Required for the value method. It must not exceed the highest flow setpoint or the circuit's maximum, and is never cut down to them; it counts as done once the read-back shows it.
data_description.hand_back_value_effect: Required with the value method: what the device does with the hand-back value — its own control resumes, or heating stops. The control switch shows it as what hand-back leads to.
data_description.hand_back_entity: For the switch method: the switch that enables external control. It is turned on when control starts and off on hand-back — so never a setting the device stores in its memory; its write type is needed below.
data_description.hand_back_entity_write_type: Needed with the switch method: what the device does with the switch's state. Expiring: dropped unless repeated — turned on again every 30 s while control holds the boiler. Held: the device keeps it — turned on once each time control takes the boiler. Persistent or unknown (default): it may be stored in the boiler's memory, which every switching would wear, so control is not available with it.

control_gateway.title: OpenTherm Gateway
control_gateway.description: The gateway set up in Home Assistant's OpenTherm Gateway integration.

data_description.gateway_id: The ID you gave the gateway in the OpenTherm Gateway integration. The control setpoint is repeated every 30 s; on hand-back it is set to 0, which returns control to the thermostat, or ends heating without one.

control_mqtt.title: OTGW firmware over MQTT
control_mqtt.description: Commands are published on the topic prefix/set/node/command, with the prefix and node name given below.

data_description.mqtt_top: The MQTT topic prefix set in the OTGW firmware. Default OTGW.
data_description.mqtt_node: The node name set in the OTGW firmware. A wrong prefix or node name sends commands nowhere; the read-back then reports them as ignored.

control_curve.title: Heating curve and limits
control_curve.description: The flow temperature the house needs at each outdoor temperature, and the limits no setpoint may pass.

data_description.design_outdoor: The coldest outdoor temperature your heating is designed for, in °C. Default: the building's design outdoor temperature, or −15 °C. Too cold a value gives too little water in frost.
data_description.design_flow: The flow temperature the heating needs at the design outdoor temperature, in °C, e.g. the value on your boiler's own curve. Required; there is no default. Too high wastes gas and makes the burner cycle; too low leaves rooms cold in hard frost.
data_description.hard_min: No setpoint below this, in °C. Default 25 °C. Too high heats rooms in mild weather and wastes gas; the "off" setpoint must stay below it.
data_description.hard_max: No setpoint above this, whatever the curve or a correction asks, in °C. Default 70 °C. Underfloor heating also needs its circuit's maximum flow.
data_description.room: The room temperature the curve is built for, in °C. Default 20 °C. Too high raises the whole curve and wastes gas.
data_description.exponent: How the curve bends. Empty picks it from the emitters: radiators 1.3, convectors 1.4, underfloor 1.1. The wrong bend under-heats in frost or overheats in mild weather.
data_description.offset: Shifts the whole curve up or down, in K. Default 0. Up wastes gas; down leaves rooms cold.
data_description.ceiling_band: How far above the curve a comfort correction may go, in K. Default 10 K; 0 turns correction off in effect. Larger lets one cold room push the water up for every room.
data_description.fallback_setpoint: Used when no outdoor temperature is known — the sensor failed, or the monitor found it stuck or far from the weather, and the weather entity is missing too — once the last effective temperature has been held for three hours, in °C. Empty (default): the curve at its design point, the most heat the curve gives: never too little heat, the valves keep rooms from overheating.
data_description.frost_limit: Any watched zone colder than this starts heating, whatever else applies, in °C. Default 5 °C. Too low risks frozen pipes; too high heats rooms you keep off.
data_description.frost_release: Frost protection ends once every watched zone is above this, in °C. Default 7 °C, above the limit. Close to the limit, frost heating starts and stops more often.
data_description.frost_zone: Optional: watch only this zone for frost. Empty (default): every zone, those Versatile Thermostat has switched off included — an unheated room below the limit then keeps frost heating on. Frost heating that does not warm the room for two hours raises an alarm; it is never stopped.

control_behaviour.title: Control behaviour
control_behaviour.description: The ramp, the decision interval, the "off" setpoint, demand thresholds and learning pauses. Heating goes on and off with Versatile Thermostat's zones, at once: nothing counted or timed holds it. Every default is the cautious one.

data_description.ramp_k_per_min: The fastest setpoint change, in K per minute. Default 1. Faster changes stress the boiler and make zones overshoot.
data_description.decision_interval_min: How often the water temperature is decided anew, in minutes; default 5, VT's default cycle. Heating on and off follows the zones at every 10 s step, whatever this is; the plugin does not read the zones' own cycles. Shorter: the water follows the weather and the rooms sooner, but the zones' algorithms see it move more often; longer: steadier water that follows more slowly.
data_description.off_setpoint: The setpoint written for "off" when there is no heating switch, in °C. Default 10: far below any heating value, and below the lowest flow setpoint. Risk: a low setpoint does not switch the boiler's heating off — ESPHome and DIYLess masters keep CH enabled, and boilers are reported to keep their CH pump running; a heating switch, or an OpenTherm Gateway's CH=0, really turns heating off.
data_description.count_threshold: Heating is needed when at least this many zones call for heat. Default 1; at most the number of zones. 0 turns the count off, leaving the power or opening threshold alone, as in Versatile Thermostat. Higher leaves a single calling room without heat.
data_description.power_threshold_kw: Optional: heating is needed when the calling zones' power, each weighted by its valve opening, adds up to this, in kW. Too high leaves small rooms without heat.
data_description.opening_threshold: Optional: heating is needed when the widest valve opening among the calling zones reaches this, in %. Too high leaves a room that opens a little without heat.
data_description.learning_pauses: Pause SmartPI learning while hot water runs, while foreign heat warms a zone and while the water temperature swings, so it does not learn what the boiler did; each pause and resume is read back from SmartPI. Default on. Auto-TPI cannot be paused without resetting what it learned, so zones running it are reported instead. Off: SmartPI learns through those moments too, which can skew its model.
data_description.comfort_correction: On (default): while a zone's valve is fully open and its room stays short of its setpoint, the water goes up to 3 K above the curve — 1 K per 30 minutes, only while heat flows — and falls twice as fast; it never rises while another zone is more than 1 K too warm, resets at hand-back, and after three hours at 3 K tells you the curve is probably too low. It acts in series with the zones' own PI (SmartPI, TPI): its slow rate lets them settle first. A zone algorithm's outdoor term (TPI's external coefficient) counts the weather a second time: keep it small while the plugin sets the water. Off: the curve alone.

control_alarms.title: Alarm reactions
control_alarms.description: What control does while an alarm is active: information only, or hand control back to the boiler until you switch control off and on again. Another controller writing to the boiler always makes the plugin step aside; it never fights it.

data.return_after_outside_change: Return by itself after another controller

data_description.return_after_outside_change: Off (default): after another controller changed the boiler twice, the plugin hands the boiler back and steps aside until you switch control off and on. On: it takes the boiler back by itself after an hour in which nothing else wrote to it. Risk: if the other controller only pauses, the two take turns; with a thermostat that keeps changing its request, the hour never passes.

control_return_confirm.title: Confirm the return by itself
control_return_confirm.description: The plugin will take the boiler back by itself an hour after another controller last wrote to it. If that controller is still there, both will control the boiler in turns. Tick to confirm.

data_description.understood: Tick to switch the return by itself on; without the tick it stays off.

error.min_power_not_below_max: The minimum power must be below the maximum power.
error.fixed_temperature_missing: A thermostatic mixing valve (fixed) needs its temperature setting.
error.foreign_heat_unsupported: Only switches, binary sensors and power or temperature sensors can be heat sources.
error.temperature_threshold_missing: A temperature source needs a temperature threshold (advanced level).
error.reference_zone_unknown: Pick one of the configured zones.
error.hand_back_value_missing: The value method needs a hand-back value.
error.hand_back_entity_missing: The switch method needs the external control switch.
error.hard_limits_out_of_order: The highest setpoint must be above the lowest.
error.frost_release_not_above_limit: Frost protection must end above the temperature where it starts.
error.hand_back_timeout_not_expiring: The device's timeout hands back only with expiring writes; choose a value or a switch.
error.hand_back_value_out_of_range: The hand-back value is outside what the setpoint entity accepts.
error.limits_outside_entity_range: The setpoint entity does not accept this limit; keep the limits within its range.
error.off_setpoint_outside_entity_range: The setpoint entity does not accept this value.
error.write_type_not_supported: The plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory: declare the setpoint entity expiring or held, or choose "No control".
error.ch_write_type_not_supported: Declare the heating switch expiring or held, or leave the switch empty: the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory.
error.hand_back_value_effect_missing: The value method needs its effect: what the device does with the hand-back value.
error.hand_back_pending: A hand-back has not reached the boiler yet: the write path, what control writes to and the gateway's read-back cannot change until it does. Bring the target back, or choose "No control": the hand-back is still retried.
error.control_holds_boiler: Control has the boiler: switch control off first, so the boiler is given back through the device that has it; then change what control writes to or the gateway's read-back.
error.count_threshold_above_zones: More zones than are configured: heating would never be asked for.
error.no_demand_criterion: Set at least one criterion: a zone count of 0 needs a power or an opening threshold.
error.off_setpoint_not_below_hard_min: "Off" must be at least 1 °C below the lowest water temperature, or the boiler would not see a change.
error.setpoint_unit_not_supported: The setpoint entity's unit is not a temperature unit (°C, °F or K): a value written would mean something else to it. Pick the boiler's flow setpoint entity.
error.implausible_parameter: A parameter is outside its plausible range.
error.unknown_circuit: A zone refers to a circuit that does not exist.
error.duplicate_circuit: Two circuits have the same name.
error.no_circuit: At least one circuit is needed.
error.invalid_control: The control settings cannot be used.
error.alarm_limits_out_of_order: An alarm limit must lie beyond its warning limit.
error.confirmed_entity_missing: Pick the entity that reports the setpoint the boiler received: every write is checked against it.
error.topology_missing: Declare how the gateway sits between thermostat and boiler: it decides what a hand-back does.
error.topology_no_control: In monitor mode the gateway only listens: control is not possible.
error.topology_not_for_path: This write path goes through a built-in OpenTherm Gateway: pick one of the gateway topologies.
error.gateway_unknown: No OpenTherm Gateway set up in Home Assistant has this ID: every write would fail.
error.mqtt_topic_invalid: Enter the topic level as the gateway's firmware uses it, without spaces or the wildcards + and #.
error.modulation_not_percent: Modulation is a percentage of the boiler's range: pick a sensor in %.
error.hand_back_entity_write_type_not_supporte: Declare the external control switch expiring or held: the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory.
error.hand_back_value_above_max: The hand-back value is above the highest flow setpoint or the circuit's maximum: the boiler would get hotter water than the circuit allows.
error.off_setpoint_near_hand_back_value: "Off" is within 0.5 K of the hand-back value, which returns the boiler to its own control: "off" would hand the boiler back instead of stopping heating. Pick another value.
error.thermostat_setpoint_same_as_read_back: Pick the thermostat's own entity, not the setpoint read-back.
error.return_needs_confirmation: Tick the box to switch this on, or go back.
error.setpoint_step_too_coarse: This entity takes values in steps above 1 °C: a rounded value would read back as ignored. Pick an entity with a finer step.

blocked_no_setpoint_entity.message: Pick the entity that takes the flow setpoint. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_no_hand_back.message: Choose how control is handed back to the boiler: a value, the device's own timeout or a switch. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_no_gateway.message: Enter the OpenTherm Gateway ID. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_vt_central_boiler_unknown.message: Versatile Thermostat's central boiler cannot be ruled out yet: VT's central configuration is not loaded (starting, reloading, or failed to load — see Settings → Devices & services). Control waits for it. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_timeout_needs_expiring_writes.message: The device's timeout hands back only with expiring writes: choose a hand-back value or a switch in the options. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_setpoint_outside_entity_range.message: The setpoint entity does not accept every value control may write (a limit, the "off" setpoint or the hand-back value): adjust them to its range in the options. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_off_setpoint_not_below_hard_min.message: The "off" setpoint is not at least 1 °C below the lowest water temperature: lower it in the options. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_hand_back_switch_not_writable.message: Declare the external control switch expiring or held: the plugin never writes to the boiler's persistent memory. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_hand_back_value_above_max.message: The hand-back value is above the highest flow setpoint or the circuit's maximum: the boiler would get hotter water than the circuit allows. Other reasons: {others}.

blocked_heating_off_ignored.message: From the start of the session the boiler did not take the plugin's "heating off", so the plugin could not switch heating off. Control stopped and the boiler was handed back. Check the heating switch picked in the options and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running. Other reasons: {others}.

auto_tpi_blocked.title: Auto-TPI cannot learn in some zones
auto_tpi_blocked.description: These zones run Auto-TPI and are marked in Versatile Thermostat as used by the central boiler, but VT's central boiler is not configured — the plugin replaces it — so Auto-TPI skips learning in them: {zones}. To let it learn, clear "used by the central boiler" in each zone's VT configuration. What that costs: the plugin cannot pause Auto-TPI without wiping what it has learned, so it will then also learn while hot water charges and while the water temperature changes, which can skew its coefficients. Leaving the option set keeps Auto-TPI's learning off in these zones.

hand_back_owed.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through

confirm.title: Handing the boiler back has not got through
confirm.description:
The plugin cannot hand the boiler back: its setpoint entity, heating switch or gateway does not take it. It retries every minute; until it gets through, the boiler may keep the last value the plugin wrote. Check that the device is available.

If you have returned the boiler to its own control by hand — or the device is gone for good — confirm here: the plugin stops retrying and forgets what it owed, and the options accept another device. Confirm only once the boiler really runs on its own.

control_options_invalid.title: The control options cannot be used
control_options_invalid.description: The saved control options cannot be used, so control is off; the monitor keeps running. The log names the option; open the options and set control up again.

control_state_unreadable.title: The plugin's memory of the boiler could not be read
control_state_unreadable.description: The file in which the plugin remembers whether it holds the boiler could not be read: it is missing or damaged (Home Assistant may show its own notice about a damaged file). To be safe, the plugin assumed it held the boiler and handed it back first. Control then works as usual; check that the boiler and the control switch are as you expect.

hand_back_owed_after_removal.title: The boiler may still hold a value from VTherm Smart Boiler
hand_back_owed_after_removal.description: The integration was removed before its hand-back reached the boiler. Return the boiler to its own control by hand — reset the setpoint entity, or clear the gateway's overrides — and then ignore this issue.

learning_not_paused.title: The plugin cannot pause learning in some zones
learning_not_paused.description: Control pauses zone learning while hot water charges, while foreign heat warms a zone and while the water temperature swings, but it cannot pause these zones: {zones}. Auto-TPI could only be paused by resetting what it learned, so the plugin leaves it alone; a SmartPI that does not publish its learning flag cannot be paused either. They keep learning through those moments, which can skew what they learn. To avoid it, stop Auto-TPI's learning in VT once it has learned, or update SmartPI — either leaves the zone without the plugin's protection until then.

vt_feature_manager_unsupported.title: VT's thermostats cannot show the plugin's zone values
vt_feature_manager_unsupported.description: The Versatile Thermostat installed here has no feature managers (they need VT 10.4 or newer, with vtherm_api 0.5 or newer), so its thermostats cannot show the plugin's hot-water and emitter values. The plugin's own zone entities show them meanwhile. Update Versatile Thermostat to show them on the thermostats too.

vt_reload_needed.title: Some VT thermostats need a reload to show the plugin's values
vt_reload_needed.description: These thermostats were already running when the plugin registered with Versatile Thermostat, and pick it up only when VT reloads: {zones}. Reload Versatile Thermostat to show the plugin's hot-water and emitter values on them; the plugin's own zone entities show them meanwhile. Nothing else depends on it.

hand_back_taken_by_other.title: After the hand-back another controller holds the boiler
hand_back_taken_by_other.description: The plugin handed the boiler back, and another controller — an automation, a device's own program or another integration — now holds what the plugin had set: {target}. The plugin counts the hand-back as done and does not write there again. With a thermostat or the boiler's own control, heating goes on under it; where the hand-back stops heating, the boiler heats only under that other controller. If you do not expect another controller, find it.

monitor_failed.title: Control handed the boiler back: the plugin's monitor keeps failing
monitor_failed.description: The plugin's monitor has failed for 5 minutes — an error in the plugin; the log has the details — so control handed the boiler back. It resumes by itself once the monitor works again. Meanwhile a thermostat or the boiler's own control heats where your installation has one; where a hand-back stops heating, the boiler does not heat until control resumes.

monitor_recovered.title: The plugin's monitor failed for a while; control has resumed
monitor_recovered.description: The plugin's monitor failed from {since} to {until}, so control handed the boiler back meanwhile. The monitor works again and control has resumed by itself. The log has the error; if this happens again, report it.

control_stopped_heating.title: Control stopped and the boiler does not heat
control_stopped_heating.description: Control handed the boiler back because something now blocks it (the control switch lists what). With this installation a hand-back stops heating: the boiler heats again when control resumes once the blocker is gone, or when you return it to its own control. Frost protection now rests on the boiler's own, if it has one.

control_latched.title: Control stepped aside: another controller writes to the boiler
control_latched.description: Another controller changed what the plugin writes to the boiler again after the plugin had written its value back once, so the plugin stepped aside and does not fight it. It handed the boiler back safely: first the lowest water temperature, then heating on where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, then the release — this wrote over the other controller's value once, briefly. With a thermostat, the thermostat keeps heating; without one, the boiler heats only under the other controller. To give control back to the plugin, stop the other controller, then switch control off and on. If "Return by itself after another controller" is on, control also comes back on its own after an hour in which nothing else wrote to the boiler (not for relays).

control_latched_heating_off_ignored.title: Control stopped: the boiler does not take "heating off"
control_latched_heating_off_ignored.description: From the start of the session the boiler did not take the plugin's "heating off", so the plugin could not switch heating off. Control stopped and handed the boiler back safely: first the lowest water temperature, then heating on where a thermostat or the boiler's own control takes over, then the release. Check the heating switch picked in the options and the boiler's settings, then switch control off and on. The monitor keeps running.
